answer: One defense anchors each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable stake: before an agent can vote or earn, it must lock a deposit and publish a cipher-signed proof tying its actions to that one deposit. Making a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, so a sybil attacker stands on a narrow ledge — each extra identity multiplies cost without multiplying influence, because rewards and voting weight are capped per anchored stake, not per account.
